tg.conclusion: Reviewed Telegram v0.117.0 to v0.123.0 with the exact published command contract. New: `account remove --keep-data|--delete-data` (logs out on Telegram's side, then forgets the profile's app id and hash, proxy password, bots' history sessions and cli-core state; a same-named bot's token stays; agents cannot start it over MCP), `models set|add`, `store import` for synthetic test stores, `schedule pause|resume` and repeatable `--at`, `muted:` in search and stats, `contracts/wirecat.json` listing the HTTP hosts. `messages sync --all` now leaves out muted chats (counted in `limited.muted`; `--with-muted` or `history_muted true` reads them), EmbeddingGemma is the default text model (219 MB, no `--accept-terms`, e5-small kept where it is the only model), an agent's `contacts link` proposes and needs `--reason`, `search messages --timeout 30s` may run about 29 seconds, `--offline` refusals answer `offline.refused` exit 5, `contacts context|prepare` read only the profile's own scope, е matches ё, BotFather's chat is kept out of search, tg's HTTP reaches only declared hosts, `serve` exits on an outdated build, and the store moves to version 63 (cli-core 0.630.0). New settings `history_muted` and `keep_store_runs_for_days`. RU/ES changelog, commands, cli-contract, configuration-reference, mcp, sessions and topic-search reviewed. Native erratum left for tg-cli: archive.md still says `messages sync --all` reads every chat. The roadmap is unchanged since v0.92.0 and none of its planned items (chat notes, emoji reaction rankings, remaining max parity, location messages) shipped.

max.conclusion: Reviewed MAX v0.103.0 to v0.111.0 with the exact published command contract. New: `account remove --keep-data|--delete-data` (ends the MAX session, then erases the token, profile files and the shared layer's data for the profile; the bot token stays; refused while `max serve` runs), `store import` (synthetic data into a test store), `schedule pause|resume`, repeatable `--at`, `participants_count` and `muted:` in search and stats, part of a name in `from:`/`chat:` (`from:Name*`), part of a word in message text (`*word*`, three letters minimum, matched as written apart from case and ё/е), and `sync.progress` events in the run record. Changed: `contacts unlink` requires `--from person:<uid>|person:me`; `--offline` on a command that needs MAX answers `permission_error` (`offline.refused`, exit 5); `contacts context|prepare` read only accounts of the profile's sphere and return `accounts`; `list:` in message search is refused (`query.unsupported-field`); remote embeddings over plain `http://` are refused off this computer (`model.address-refused`); `search messages --timeout` can run up to 29 seconds; test-data people are hidden from people lists; a damaged store answers `configuration_error` (`store.damaged`) and blocks writes; the store moves to version 66 (cli-core 0.642.0, cli-base 0.96.0). Fixed: `messages sync --all` reports progress inside a chat, daily and one-time schedules wait out `rate_limited` up to six hours, `max serve` exits with code 3 when outdated so systemd starts the new version, and setting the clock back no longer blocks sync. Topic search now defaults to `embeddinggemma` (`--accept-terms` is a no-op). RU commands copy and EN/ES bot, changelog, cli-contract, commands, mcp, people, sessions, topic-search, troubleshooting and usage reviewed (pinned source links moved to v0.111.0). Native gaps left for max-cli: query-language.md does not describe the new search syntax (`*part*`, `from:Name*`, `muted:`, `list:` refused), the changelog does not name the topic-search model change, and empty-default option rows still print a pair of backticks. The roadmap is unchanged since v0.76.0; none of its planned items shipped.

zm.conclusion: Reviewed Zoom v0.67.0 to v0.71.0 with the exact published command contract. New: `zm app` prints the Zoom app checklist (`--json`), `session end` deletes the saved login and keeps meetings, `account remove --keep-data|--delete-data` (refused while an archive schedule runs; does not revoke at Zoom), `meetings sync --rescan`, and `meetings sync` stops before `--timeout` and resumes (`stopped`, `remaining`). `meetings export` works read-only and over MCP without `--output`. `session start --json --answer-stdin` asks for `client_id`, and a sign-in with no app fails with `zoom.client-id-missing`. `search all` drops `--max-meetings`: it reads the profile's meetings through the search index, ranked with other sources, at most 3 hits per meeting, with `cue_ref` on transcript hits, and never builds the index. An agent's `meetings link` becomes a proposal (cli-core 0.619.0), while the owner's `--yes` applies at once. `--offline` refusals use `offline.refused` exit 5, and the store moves to schema 57. RU/ES changelog, commands, search and zoom-app reviewed. docs/sessions.md still says there is no logout command, so a reviewed portal correction names `session end` and `account remove` in EN/RU/ES; the search.md `zm_write` correction stays. The authored Meetings guide (EN/RU/ES) was checked against v0.71.0 commands, flags and fields and needed no change, so its pin moves to v0.71.0. The roadmap is unchanged: audio recording of attended calls, notes/speaker naming, broader preparation and additional platforms remain planned; none shipped.

drive.conclusion: Reviewed drive 0.62.0 to 0.65.0 from the changelog and the docs diff since v0.61.0. Added: `drive documents add <url> --profiles <a,b|all>` keeps one Drive document's text in the shared store as a source added by hand, for memo's Add to memory. It tries the named profiles in order, at most `max_add_profiles` (default 5, at most 50), moves on only after an access refusal, answers `duplicate_of` for a file a sync already imported, and does not run over MCP. Also added: `account remove --keep-data|--delete-data`, `folders browse [--parent]`, and `schedule pause|resume`. May break callers: a profile with no saved sign-in fails with `oauth.missing`, not `oauth.expired`. `memories add --supersedes` retires the old memory only once the owner confirms. The shared store moves to version 57 and then, on cli-core 0.634.0, to 64. Fixed: a document's owner and last editor no longer land in your memory or its review, and a spent Google quota is a rate limit, not a permission refusal. RU/ES changelog (kept in English, as before), commands, configuration and usage reviewed. Since `documents add` ships, the memo troubleshooting correction that worked around it was retired. The roadmap is unchanged since v0.61.0: its Next item, `mirrors watch` as a background service, has not shipped.

Digests by name (`digest list|add|edit|run|pause|resume|remove`, `backfill --since-time|--until-time`). `sources add` reads an image with the chosen AI model, and `sources preview` shows a page before adding it. Also `models ai` and `models local-only`, `records import` from a CSV sheet, `stats projects show`, and `groups update --scope`. wa.conclusion: Reviewed WhatsApp v0.30.0 to v0.38.0 from the changelog and the source diff. wa now asks WhatsApp at most 20 times a minute per profile, 10 at once (was 60 and 20), and `messages sync <chat>` asks the phone for a page every 5 to 10 seconds; `--pause` of `messages download --all`, `attachments download` and `store gaps repair` defaults to 5s. `session start` waits for the phone's own signal that its history sync is done (five minutes of quiet at most), `session start phone --json --answer-stdin` lets a window such as WireCat Desktop link by pairing code, the QR event carries `expires_at`, and `--json` reports the pairing code and the history wait as events. `account remove --keep-data|--delete-data` unlinks a profile and forgets it. `contacts add` and `contacts rename` save a WhatsApp contact name (remove and import stay refused); `contacts unlink` needs `--from`, `contacts context` reads only the asked account's scope. Queries gain name patterns in `from:` and `chat:`, `*part*` inside words, `participants_count` and `muted:`; `store import` loads a synthetic test store; `serve` exits when its build is out of date; `--offline` on a networked command is refused with `offline.refused`. From cli-core the reference also gains `models set`, `models add` (`--accept-terms` no longer needed), embeddinggemma as the default model, `search all --only meetings` without `--max-meetings`, `contacts link --reason`, bot `--button` and `--no-buttons`, `messages sync --with-muted` with `history_muted`, `keep_store_runs_for_days`, `owner_languages` and the `crm.*` settings. RU/ES changelog (0.31.0 to 0.38.0), commands (English body, as before), archive, attachments, configuration-reference, limits, people, query-language, sessions and usage reviewed; the RU query-language `kind` row's wrong wording was corrected. No correction changed. Upstream errata left for whatsapp-cli: sessions and archive still say `session start` stops after 45 seconds of quiet, and the changelog does not say that `messages sync --all` now leaves muted chats out. The roadmap is unchanged and none of its planned items shipped.

gcal.conclusion: Reviewed gcal 0.22.0 and 0.23.0 from the changelog and the command diff since v0.21.0. 0.23.0 adds `account remove --keep-data|--delete-data`, which revokes the Google sign-in and forgets the profile, `models set` and `models add` from cli-core, and `contracts/wirecat.json` naming the hosts gcal talks to. Every request to Google now goes through cli-base's hostFetch, which refuses any other host. The store moves to version 59. 0.22.0 moves the store to version 57 and reads a store a newer memo already moved. `upgrade --offline` and `calendars busy --offline` answer `permission_error` `offline.refused` (exit 5). `events prepare` reads only accounts of the asked account's scope. Search reads a trailing `?` and an unknown `word:` as words, and ё matches е in names. It also corrects the 0.21.0 note about WireCat's Google app. RU/ES changelog and commands reviewed. The roadmap's Next is now that nothing new is planned yet, since everything it listed has shipped; the RU/ES roadmap already said so. Earlier: Reviewed released Google Calendar 0.21.0 (Core 0.600.0/Base 0.80.8). 0.21.0 adds schedule --notify-on and --deliver-to (schedule agent also --model and --max-cost-per-day), and session start --client-id with the google_client_id setting to choose your own Google app (order: --client-file or --client-id, GCAL_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, the profile's then the defaults' google_client_id, WireCat's app; the secret only from GCAL_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET; config set refuses google_client_id to an agent). A write cut short by Ctrl-C ends as outcome_unknown (exit 14), not cancelled. Security: every api events method also checks the key of the matching events command, reads included, on --dry-run, api show (also_checks) and MCP, and a patch to cancelled also checks events.delete; checked on the 0.21.0 build with an isolated profile, no sign-in: api show calendar.events.delete lists also_checks events.delete, and api calendar-events-delete --dry-run is refused with access.denied once events.delete is deny. mcp serve --permission api.<method>=deny now stops the events writes that call that method. A Google call no longer holds the finished command for 30 seconds. gcal's own installation, configuration, usage, troubleshooting and roadmap pages now say every package carries WireCat's Google app and that Google may refuse a sign-in through it, so the five 0.20.0 portal corrections for those pages are retired; the changelog correction for 0.20.0's two old reason names stays, since that section is unchanged. One new EN correction rewords "unset the secret to use WireCat's app" in troubleshooting, which docs:versions read as an editorial phrase. EN/RU/ES pages reviewed: changelog (RU/ES 0.21.0 section), commands (--client-id; copied from the released reference), configuration (the sign-in order list, the events keys the api methods also need), installation (WireCat's app in every package, --client-id, google_client_id), troubleshooting (the oauth_client null row, the missing-secret row, the unverified app row), usage (the sign-in order). Index, remote, scenarios and security unchanged. Roadmap: v0.21.0 dropped its only Next item (sign-in without your own client, shipped in 0.20.0) and listed no status, so the roadmap page is pinned to gcal-cli main 8167d16 (gcal-cli #133), which says nothing new is planned yet. The comparison page is checked against 0.21.0 on 7 November: no mark changes; the agent-permission note adds that the raw api events methods answer to the same events keys. Earlier: Reviewed released Google Calendar 0.20.0 (Core 0.566.0/Base 0.77.1). 0.20.0 renames error reasons to the names cli-core and drive share (sign-in.expired is oauth.expired, sign-in.scope-missing and api.scope-missing are oauth.scope-missing, profile.not-signed-in is oauth.missing, google.denied is access.denied, google.not-found is item.not-found, google.usage-limit is provider.usage-limit). calendars busy takes and answers starts_at and ends_at. A sync where one calendar fails saves and answers the others with meta.complete false and a sync.partial issue, exit 0. cli-core 0.566.0 adds the conflict failure (exit 15), and doctor connects nowhere unless doctor --online. gcal signs in with WireCat's Google app from cli-core's constants.json with no client file (order: --client-file, then GCAL_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GCAL_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, then WireCat's app), a secret without an id fails with sign-in.secret-without-id, sign-in.no-client and sign-in.bundled-client-invalid are gone, and doctor's oauth_client is {client, source}. Also: config migrate and config repair, events create --text retries with --operation-id, session start opens no browser under --json, --no-input or CI, reads open the store read-only, Google paging stops after a repeated token or 1000 pages, events export --output writes a private file whole, organizer-only changes say event.organizer-only, local times at a terminal, and busy says when Google did not answer. EN/RU/ES pages reviewed: changelog (RU/ES translated), commands (calendars busy fields, doctor --online, config migrate and repair, exit 15), usage (partial sync, busy fields, quick add retry), remote (the example tunnel address), troubleshooting (oauth.scope-missing). gcal's own installation, configuration, usage, troubleshooting and roadmap pages at v0.20.0 still say releases do not carry WireCat's app, so portal corrections in EN/RU/ES now say every package carries it, that Google has not verified it yet (unverified app page, 100 users in total shared with drive), and that your own app is the way out. Troubleshooting drops the rows for errors 0.20.0 cannot give (unreadable bundled client, no client set up, oauth_client.client null), adds sign-in.secret-without-id. The owner confirmed a real sign-in through WireCat's app with the Calendar API on, so the pages drop the hedges that doubted it. The changelog correction names oauth.missing and provider.usage-limit where 0.20.0's Fixed section still names the old reasons. The comparison adds a row for following a calendar published as an .ics address (gcal yes, the other tools not in their documentation), keeps one search over meetings, chats, mail and notes as partly because mail goes to memo search mail, adds schedule to the reminders note, a calendar feeds note, and names calendars add, remove and schedule among the commands kept at a terminal. Earlier: Reviewed released Google Calendar 0.14.0 (Core 0.543.0/Base 0.73.0), covering 0.13.0. 0.13.0: events list, events prepare, doctor and session status carry meta.now, meta.now_local and meta.timezone (WC-TIME-7), and the skill tells the agent to plan from them; over MCP a list's query names its fields and says -event_type:<kind> or NOT event_type:<kind> leaves a kind out; events export without --output runs through gcal_read, so a read-only profile (GCAL_READ_ONLY) can export, while --output stays off MCP and the read-only lock refuses it. 0.14.0: events remind [--due-within 10m, 1m to 1d] [--dry-run] [--offline] [-- <program> ...], for cron, a systemd timer, launchd or Task Scheduler, syncs, then tells once about each timed event that starts within the window (not cancelled, declined, focus, out-of-office or working-location; a moved meeting is reminded again); a failed sync still reminds from the store with meta.complete: false and exits with the sync's code. The program runs with no shell, once per event, the event as one JSON line on stdin with ref and untrusted, GCAL_EVENT and GCAL_PROFILE in its environment; exit 0 marks it reminded, any other leaves it for the next run (remind.hook-failed), 60 seconds stops it, and a second run at once answers remind.running. permissions.events.remind.hook defaults to deny, --yes does not lift it, GCAL_READ_ONLY refuses it, and no MCP tool offers events remind. RU/ES changelog, usage (Get reminded before a meeting, the time in answers, export through gcal_read), commands, security and roadmap reviewed; scenarios unchanged. The comparison adds a row for a reminder through your own program (gcal and gcalcli yes) and notes on the time in answers, reminders and their safety rules, and read-only export; three commands now stay off MCP. Roadmap changed: What works today names events remind; Next is still only sign-in through WireCat's shared Google app. Earlier: Reviewed released Google Calendar 0.12.0 (Core 0.539.0/Base 0.71.0). events prepare [event:<id>] gives the stored evidence for one meeting, the next one when none is named (timed, not cancelled or declined, not focus, out-of-office or working-location, with someone else invited): the event with attendees' answers and Drive files, and per attendee linked identities, latest one-to-one messages and mail, group messages, past events and recorded meetings from every WireCat tool on the computer; it reads the store only and writes no summary, meta.complete: false names chat.not-read or meetings.index-pending, untrusted marks other people's text. The skill and gcal guide gain prepare-meeting and digest. events create --text hands one line to Google's quickAdd (keys events.create and api.calendar.events.quickAdd, no --operation-id). events export <query> [--output file.ics] writes up to 1000 events in UTC, one per occurrence; events import <calendar> <file> adds up to 500 events under their UIDs through events.import, mails nobody and asks first (events.import ask). events list takes event_type:<kind> and -event_type:<kind> (the only field a minus can leave out) and id:<id>; calendars are named by title everywhere, a shared name refused with calendar.ambiguous. RU/ES changelog, usage, commands and scenarios (new digest and prepare-meeting) reviewed; the comparison marks preparing for the next meeting as yes and adds rows for leaving out birthdays and working-location blocks and for .ics export and import. Roadmap unchanged since 0.7.0: sign-in through WireCat's shared Google app is still planned. Earlier: Reviewed released Google Calendar 0.11.0 (Core 0.527.0/Base 0.68.1). events list --source reads several accounts as one list (all, a provider, gcal:<profile>,... or group:<name>): meta.accounts names them, a meeting two accounts hold is listed once, an account with no synced calendar or an unfinished sync makes the answer partial (meta.complete: false, calendar.unsynced or calendar.sync-incomplete), and GCAL_PROFILE_LOCK limits --source to the locked profile. events list overlapping:true keeps timed meetings that overlap another, each with overlaps; cancelled, declined, free, working-location and all-day events are left out and back-to-back meetings do not overlap; with --source it compares across accounts. session start can use a WireCat Google app built into the package, but 0.11.0 carries none, so every user still makes their own: the installation guide gains Make your own Google app (steps 1 to 8) and troubleshooting gains Sign-in problems. The usage guide's raw api section now matches 0.7.0 (easy-to-undo writes run without a question, deletes and sharing ask, calendars.clear, delete and transferOwnership refused until allowed). The MCP server is listed in the MCP Registry as dev.wirecat/gcal-cli from the next release. RU/ES installation, configuration, troubleshooting, usage, commands and changelog reviewed; the comparison marks all accounts in one list and overlapping meetings as yes. Roadmap unchanged since 0.7.0: sign-in through WireCat's shared Google app is still planned, and no release carries that app yet. Earlier: Reviewed released Google Calendar 0.10.0 (Core 0.512.0/Base 0.68.1). 0.10.0 only moves gcal to cli-core 0.512.0: no command, option, setting or MCP input changes for gcal. cli-core 0.512.0 renamed id to operation_id in its shared calendar MCP tools and gave events_list a page, but gcal does not serve those tools; its agents use gcal_write and gcal_read, which already take operation_id and events list --page since 0.9.0. Earlier: Reviewed released Google Calendar 0.9.0 (Core 0.510.0/Base 0.68.1), covering 0.8.0. 0.8.0 takes the keyring's file fallback from cli-base 0.68.0 with no workaround of gcal's own: a sign-in in the private file stays there until a session start reaches the keyring again. 0.9.0 renames events create --id and events update --following --id to --operation-id (may break callers), adds events list --page with a page.next step that keeps the query, makes search events --backend both answer (store hits first, those Google also found marked server, then Google-only hits, one page with no cursor), fixes the --cursor help, and the MCP agent log now names the calling agent instead of gcal-mcp. mail.conclusion: Reviewed mail 0.29.0 to 0.32.0 from the changelog and the command diff since v0.28.0. 0.29.0: `rules apply` runs up to 15 minutes by default in a terminal and 45 seconds over MCP, reads headers newest first and saves batch by batch; a run that reaches its limit answers `state: partial` with a cursor, and `rules apply --cursor` goes on from there; `rules apply` takes `--yes` over MCP; `score:` and `--kind` judge a sender from the store; the time-limit error names the time limit. 0.30.0 builds on cli-core 0.659.0 and mends a shared config with a small slip, keeping a `.bak` copy. 0.31.0: `rules import --format gmail` takes its own `--yes` over MCP, `rules export` answers over MCP, a resumed `rules apply` that read nothing points to `MAIL_TIMEOUT` over MCP or adds `--timeout 30m` in a terminal, and `messages delete --rules` keeps mail from senders the owner wrote to. 0.32.0: a `readonly` level no longer stops `mail sync`; `deny` still does. RU/ES changelog and commands reviewed. The Email guide and the Yandex Telemost page were checked against the new behaviour: neither says `rules apply` needs a long `--timeout`, fails on a big mailbox or that `readonly` stops sync, so both stay unchanged; the pin moves to v0.32.0. The roadmap is unchanged since v0.17.0: its Next item, a live test of Gmail over OAuth, is not claimed as done. Earlier: Reviewed mail 0.25.0 to 0.28.0 from the changelog and the command diff since v0.24.0. `rules add --do meeting-notes:<provider>` keeps the matched mail whole and protected and saves it as a meeting on sync; `rules apply --yes` saves notes stored before the rule, and its dry run counts them. Telemost notes in Yandex's older layout take the text before the first heading as their summary, and the footer is not stored. `doctor reports show|create`, the `crm.<provider>:<account>.activities` setting, the local-only model switch, declared hosts, and sync on a fresh install with an unreadable shared config. RU/ES changelog and commands reviewed. The Email guide does not describe any of these and stays correct; its pin moves to v0.28.0. The new Yandex Telemost page documents the meeting-notes rule. The roadmap is unchanged since v0.17.0: its Next item, a live test of Gmail over OAuth, is not claimed as done.

b24.conclusion: Reviewed b24 v0.15.0 with its published changelog and the changed command reference, usage and troubleshooting pages. 0.15.0 adds account remove (cli-core's shared command, --keep-data or --delete-data, refused while another profile reads the same portal), a local task when a deal or lead enters a stage named in stage-tasks, shell completion, the shared store's file commands and doctor reports, and an update notice. session start refuses a webhook another profile already uses, and a webhook without user_basic says what to tick. A sync with no users chosen now copies the signed-in user's own deals and leads instead of stopping with configuration_error, which WireCat Desktop showed as config.invalid; a chosen list replaces that user. A stored scope all names bitrix.scope-all-refused, and a lead keeps its own person and company names. The roadmap is unchanged since v0.14.0: its Next items, contacts and companies from the local store and their custom fields kept locally, have not shipped. RU/ES changelog, commands, troubleshooting and usage translated and accepted.

pbx.conclusion: First publication of the Asterisk CLI (pbx) at v0.3.0, with its 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 notes. 0.3.0 renames the command to pbx, also wcat-pbx, with PBX_ variables and pbx_ MCP tools, while the package, settings folder and keyring keep the asterisk-cli name. 0.2.0 adds files_from sftp with a pinned server key and fixes phone_region for every country. The roadmap is the tool's own: missed-call and direction filters, call statistics, transfer legs shown together and the CEL log are planned, none shipped. RU/ES translations of every page accepted.
